title: Sensible Use of Capitals
statement:
You get a word made of English letters. Its capitals are used sensibly if exactly one of these is true:

  • every letter is uppercase, like "HTML",
  • every letter is lowercase, like "div",
  • only the first letter is uppercase, like "Seoul".

Return true if the word uses capitals sensibly, otherwise false.

examples.why: Only the first letter is a capital.
One capital, but not in first place. Counting capitals alone is not enough; their position matters.
The first letter is a capital, but so are others, and not all of them.

hints: How many capital letters can a sensible word have?
Count the capitals. Zero is fine, all of them is fine. What about exactly one?
Exactly one capital is fine only if it is the first letter. Any other count is not sensible.

explain.intuition:
The three allowed shapes are all about how many capitals there are and where they sit. Count the uppercase letters in one pass. If the count is 0 (all lowercase) or equal to the word's length (all uppercase), the word is fine. If the count is exactly 1, it is fine only when that one capital is the first letter.

Any other count, like two capitals in a five-letter word, fails all three rules. A one-letter word always passes, since its single letter is either lowercase or the first letter.
steps: Count the uppercase letters in word as caps.
If caps === 1 and the first letter is uppercase, return true.
pitfalls: Accepting any word with exactly one capital. "iPhone" has one capital but in the wrong place.
Checking only the first two letters to decide the case of the rest, then not checking the rest. "ABc" starts like an all-caps word but is not one.
Requiring the three shapes to be exclusive. A one-letter capital like "Q" fits both "all caps" and "first letter only", and it is fine.

solutions.title: Compare with the three allowed shapes
solutions.idea: Build the all-upper, all-lower and capitalized versions of the word and check whether the word equals one of them.

solutions.title: Count capitals
solutions.idea: Zero capitals or all capitals is fine. Exactly one is fine only in first place.

followups: Check a whole sentence word by word, where words are separated by spaces.
Return the word fixed to the closest sensible form instead of true or false. What does "closest" mean?
